Diagnosed and verified. The solution is in **`~/red-attribution/SOLUTION.md`**, with the working script and tests alongside it.

## Summary

**Root cause (two layers of the same disease):**

1. **Parser bug.** `curl … | jq -r '.[].id'` discards the HTTP status and makes jq index whatever body came back. On `401/403/404`, `/pipelines` returns a JSON **object** (`{"message":"401 Unauthorized"}`), so jq throws `Cannot index string with string "id"`. The auth error is misread as a pipeline result.
2. **Misattribution.** A job can report `status=failed` without ever executing. The "never ran" fingerprint is `failure_reason=stuck_or_timeout_failure`, `duration=0`, `started_at=null`, with later stages `skipped`, and a runner that is `active=true` but `status=stale`/`online=false`/`contacted_at=null`. That is an **infra runner outage**, not a code defect.

**Exact fix:** the safe request pattern (`-o file` + `-w '%{http_code}'`, assert `type=="array"` before jq) plus `gitlab-red-attribution.sh`, which applies the discriminator and exits `0`=blocked/infra, `10`=code-defect, `20`=not-red, `30`=needs-triage, `40`=API error. Only a failed job with `started_at != null` counts as a code defect.

**Verification:** a mock GitLab API reproduces the exact `jq` error and all four scenarios pass:

```
PASS  bash -n syntax
PASS  shellcheck
PASS  unauthenticated object is detected, not mis-jq-ed (exit=40)
PASS  runner outage -> blocked/infra (exit=0)
PASS  executed failure -> code defect (exit=10)
PASS  empty pipelines -> clean API error (exit=40)
PASS=4 FAIL=0
```

The incident fixture (`pipeline 4078`, lint `42253` stuck, runners `42254–42257` skipped, runner `3` stale) produces `VERDICT: blocked (INFRA / runner outage)` with instructions to record **blocked** and not file a code-defect row — matching the verified 2026-11-15 case.

signatures.description: HOW TO ATTRIBUTE A GITLAB PIPELINE RED TO A RUNNER OUTAGE (not a code failure). RECIPE (all read-only): 1) curl -sS -H "PRIVATE-TOKEN: $GITLAB_TOKEN" "https://HOST/api/v4/projects/<urlencoded-path>/pipelines?ref=<branch>&per_page=8" -> write to a FILE with -o and print -w 'http=%{http_code}'; never pipe straight into jq (an auth/404 error body is a JSON object, so jq -r '.[].id' fails with 'Cannot index string with string "id"'). 2) curl .../pipelines/<id>/jobs -> for each job read .status, .failure_reason, .duration, .started_at. 3) curl .../runners?per_page=20 -> for the runner(s) read .active, .status, .online, .contacted_at. DISCRIMINATOR: a runner outage looks like status=failed with failure_reason=stuck_or_timeout_failure, duration=0, started_at=null on the FIRST stage job (e.g. lint) while all later-stage jobs (build/test/e2e/docker) are skipped, plus runner active=true but status=stale / online=false / contacted_at=null. That combination proves the job was never executed, so the red is infra, not code: record it as blocked with the runner fact, do NOT file a code-defect row. VERIFIED 2026-11-15 on totalwindup/heading: pipeline 4078 (master 387d0357) failed, lint job 42253 failure_reason=stuck_or_timeout_failure duration=0 started_at=null, runners 42254-42260 all skipped, runner 3 heading-docker-runner active=true status=stale online=false contacted_at=null.
signatures.environment: self-hosted GitLab (gitlab.readydedis.com), API v4, PRIVATE-TOKEN header
